engine_best.meaning: Paragraphs 1, 2 and 4 are the original verbatim. Paragraph 3 changes "across the nation" to "across the mob" and "the people" to "the battlers"; "battlers" means struggling ordinary workers, so the tour now connects NASA with the working poor rather than people generally. The closing "Well, I'll be buggered." is an invented reaction hanging off nothing in particular. Facts, dates and names all survive.
engine_best.sense: Of the three Aussie substitutions, "across the mob" takes the wrong sense outright (a mob is a group of people or animals, not a country), and "the battlers" narrows people to struggling working folk. "Well, I'll be buggered." expresses astonishment, which nothing in the text sets up.
engine_best.authenticity: It is an American press release with Australian words dropped in: "connect the agency with the battlers, technologies, and organisations" and "With stops across the mob" are things no Australian would say. The US forms "Oct. 11", "10 a.m. to 1 p.m. EDT" and "Tailgate Zone" phrasing stay untouched; only "organisations" and "honour" are respelt. The stock tag "Well, I'll be buggered." is bolted on.
engine_best.register: The brief is level 4, close to a full pub yarn, but three of four paragraphs are untouched corporate prose ("convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders", "will showcase the next-generation aircraft"). Vulgarity is within level 1 ("buggered"). Far lighter than asked.
engine_best.tone: The original's upbeat promotional tone survives because the text is mostly unchanged, but the closing "Well, I'll be buggered." reads as baffled surprise, which jars with the announcement.
engine_best.flow: Mostly reads as the original, but "With stops across the mob" and "Now, the tour will culminate" are clunky joins, and "Well, I'll be buggered." lands with no lead-in after a long formal sentence.
engine_best.variety: Only four touches in total: "mob", "battlers", "Now," and "Well, I'll be buggered." Nothing repeats, but there is almost nothing to vary.
engine_best.essence: Unmistakably the original because it is the original almost word for word; nothing of it has been retold in an Australian voice.

unharnessed.meaning: Every fact survives: Isaacman flying "one of three F-5 fighter jets", the game, place and "Sunday, the 11th of October"; the Experience Zone "from 10 in the mornin' till 1 in the arvo, Eastern Daylight Time"; the Artemis dome, games and "blow-up SLS (Space Launch System) rocket"; the tour's stakeholders ("the uni types, the industry crowd and the public sector folks"); MAX POWER dates and Kennedy location, the 250th, and the showcase list. Additions such as "the big boss of the whole show" and "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh? Even if it's their funny American version with all the helmets and padding." are colour hanging off the original. "driverless vehicles" for autonomous vehicles is a fair gloss.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit their contexts: "having a yarn with the punters" for engaging fans, "rock up", "have a crack at", "happy snaps", "blow-up" for inflatable, "outfits" for organisations, "bring-the-kids-along kind of do" for family-friendly, "getting about" for transportation. "the footy" for American football is knowingly qualified in the next sentence.
unharnessed.authenticity: Largely natural: "rock up", "happy snaps", "uni types", "a bring-the-kids-along kind of do" are how Australians talk. Some stock lines are bolted on: "Righto, get a load of this.", "Ripper." as a standalone tag, and "Strewth, it'll be a beauty." "is gonna jump in the cockpit" uses the US-leaning "gonna".
unharnessed.register: A proper level-4 yarn throughout ("Righto, get a load of this.", "from 10 in the mornin' till 1 in the arvo") without tipping into incoherence. Swearing stays at level 1: "the bloody Moon", "bloody massive".
unharnessed.tone: The original's upbeat, promotional enthusiasm is carried as a mate's excitement: "Not a bad way to start the footy, eh?", "a ripper of a finale", "Strewth, it'll be a beauty." Appropriate shift for the brief; nothing inverted.
unharnessed.flow: Reads aloud well; long sentences are broken naturally. Small bumps: "America's big 250th birthday, a historic one" is an awkward afterthought, and "bloody Moon" then "bloody massive" in the same sentence clunks.
unharnessed.variety: Wide range of slang ("punters", "rock up", "have a crack", "happy snaps", "outfits", "do", "arvo"), but "bloody" appears twice in one sentence and "ripper" twice ("Ripper." and "a ripper of a finale").
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the NASA Inspiration Tour announcement, retold as a yarn: the administrator flying a jet, the tailgate experience, the tour's purpose and the MAX POWER finale all present, with a wry Aussie aside on gridiron.
